cpu.title: CPU · central processing unit
cpu.text: The general-purpose processor: it runs your program, prepares data, and coordinates the rest of the computer. Multiple cores can work on separate tasks at the same time.
cpu.tidbit: More cores help parallel work, but a task that must happen one step at a time may still depend on the speed of a single core.

gpu.title: GPU · graphics processing unit
gpu.text: Originally built for graphics, GPUs are also good at doing many similar calculations at once—useful for neural networks, image processing, and some simulations.
gpu.tidbit: Software has to support the GPU. Simply having one does not make every program faster. An integrated GPU usually shares system RAM rather than having its own separate memory.

memory.title: RAM · random-access memory
memory.text: The computer’s temporary workspace for running programs and their data. More RAM lets larger datasets fit in memory, but it is not the same thing as disk storage.
memory.tidbit: Capacity tells you how much fits; bandwidth tells you how quickly data can move. RAM normally loses its contents when the computer powers off.

vram.title: VRAM · GPU memory
vram.text: The GPU’s own workspace for model weights, images, intermediate results, and other data. A workload must fit here or deliberately move or split its data.
vram.tidbit: Training needs room for more than model weights: gradients, optimizer state, and intermediate activations also use memory.

npu.title: NPU · neural processing unit
npu.text: A specialized processor for supported AI tasks, often designed for efficient on-device inference—running an already-trained model.
npu.tidbit: An NPU is not a small general-purpose GPU. The model, operators, and software runtime must support it.

discrete.title: Discrete · a separate graphics processor
discrete.text: A GPU separate from the CPU, typically on its own graphics card with its own memory. It handles supported graphics and parallel computation.
discrete.tidbit: “Discrete” means separate. It does not specify a brand, memory capacity, or software compatibility.

interconnect.title: PCIe · Peripheral Component Interconnect Express
interconnect.text: A high-speed connection used to move data between the computer and devices such as graphics cards and SSDs. Think of it as a road between components, not another processor.
interconnect.tidbit: PCIe connections have generations and lane counts (such as x16). Both affect available bandwidth; transferring data can still take time even with a fast GPU.
